context_facts.fact: Egypt’s official tourism portal describes Hurghada as a global tourist destination with year-round sunshine, coral reefs, coastline, beach resorts, water sports, and a marina.
The official tourism portal identifies the Giftun Islands as an island-life attraction off Hurghada with crystal-blue water and white sandy beaches.
The supplied route registry contains canonical Hurghada-area route IDs, but its fare values are proxy tiers rather than exact Egypt-native one-way scheduled fares.
Egypt’s official tourism portal locates El Gouna 25 km north of Hurghada and describes world-class marinas, winding canals and lagoons, beaches, sailing, and other amenities.
El Gouna’s official Abu Tig Marina page describes yacht berthing, boat rentals, metered electricity/water, wastewater pump-out, fuel, 24-hour security, and dry storage for over 100 boats.

The existing Hurghada–El Gouna registry record is a 14 nm corridor, but its demand is a modeled guest-pool haircut and its fare is explicitly a Dubai premium placeholder; neither should be treated as an Egypt-native production fare.

Egypt’s official tourism portal places Sharm El Sheikh between Ras Muhammad National Park and the Nabq Protectorate and highlights its reefs, beaches, hotels, resorts, and international airport connectivity.
Official inDrive copy specifically frames Sharm journeys to beaches and resorts, supporting a ground-to-water distribution narrative without proving marine demand.

Supplied files contain canonical IDs for Sharm marina, Landmark Marina, Sharks Bay, and Ras Mohammed links; two IDs share Landmark–Sharks Bay endpoints and require canonical reconciliation before economics.
Official inDrive Cairo page establishes current city ride service and lists Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh among Egypt service areas.
No exact marine boarding-point, canonical route ID, or route-level demand/fare evidence for Cairo was established in this pass.
